page: Amazon Web Services m3.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 30.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 3.75 GB per core. It includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates moderate multi-core capabilities alongside weaker single-core performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Passmark CPU score both rank in the average tier, while Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores fall into the poor and weak categories respectively. Memory bandwidth remains stable, with uncached read speeds at 49.24 GB/sec and write speeds at 35.54 GB/sec, both registering as average. However, database operations and Redis SET performance are weak to poor, with Redis achieving 2.86 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m3.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density of compute, memory, and bundled NVMe storage, though its legacy hardware architecture limits its performance in modern, instruction-heavy workloads. It lacks support for advanced instruction sets like AVX-512. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves an average throughput of 6.7 GB/sec, software compilation, and legacy application hosting that do not demand high single-core throughput or intensive database transaction rates.
